title: First printing, expansion prototype and reprint

threads.title: Moss Market first print run
threads.scope: Finalize components, proof, manufacture and receive the first 300-copy commercial print run of Moss Market.

threads.title: Moss Market night-market expansion prototype
threads.scope: Independently prototype and evaluate an optional night-market expansion before deciding whether to produce it.

threads.title: Moss Market second print order
threads.scope: Fulfill a separately commissioned 500-copy reprint order for a retailer after the first print job closes.

threads.title: Desk lamp rewiring
threads.scope: Replace the damaged cord of a desk lamp and verify the repair.

captures.text: Two millimeters more around the cards.
captures.rationale: An isolated dimension fragment does not identify a box, prototype or job.

captures.text: Moss Market first commercial print order: 300 copies. Finalize the base-game tray, approve proofs and receive the finished cartons under this job.
captures.rationale: Defines one print undertaking from component work to receipt.

captures.text: Night-market expansion is an independent Moss Market prototype. Test whether after-dark trading adds useful choices; do not include these cards in the first print order.
captures.rationale: Distinct exploratory goal and explicit exclusion establish a separate project.

captures.text: Desk lamp photo description: cord insulation split at the base grommet. Keep the lamp unplugged while replacing its lead.
captures.rationale: A household lamp repair has no supported game-production connection.

captures.text: My two-millimeter note was about card clearance in the base-game tray for Moss Market's first 300-copy print job. It did not concern expansion cards.
captures.rationale: Explicitly resolves the early fragment to the first print order.

captures.text: First-print tray proof test: sleeved base-game cards lift out without bending after the extra clearance. The token wells still hold their contents when tilted.
captures.rationale: Tests the clarified component revision for the first printing.

captures.text: Night-market expansion playtest report: bidding after dark slowed the final round. Revise the prototype's turn limit before another independent test.
captures.rationale: Results and revision continue the expansion experiment.

captures.text: Retailer has separately commissioned a 500-copy Moss Market reprint, with its own invoice and shipment. Planning can start now; manufacturing waits for the first job to close.
captures.rationale: A separate order establishes a distinct repeat manufacturing undertaking.

captures.text: Printer account statement: deposit and balance for Moss Market's first 300-copy order; separate deposit for the retailer's 500-copy reprint. Do not combine the shipments.
captures.rationale: The statement directly covers two separately commissioned print jobs.

captures.text: Delivery docket: all 300 Moss Market first-run copies received, tray proof accepted, no carton damage. First manufacturing job closed.
captures.rationale: Receipt and closure complete the first print run.

captures.text: Retailer reprint stock quote: 500 Moss Market boxes using the accepted base-game tray specification; offer thicker cover paper for this second order only.
captures.rationale: Reusing a specification does not erase the second order's separate scope.

captures.text: Second night-market prototype session: the shorter turn limit worked, but the group wants clearer bidding icons. Keep this result with expansion research, not either print order.
captures.rationale: A follow-up test belongs to the expansion's continuing experiment.

events.reason: c05 identifies the dimension as first-print base-game tray clearance. Assign my fragment to that print job.

events.text: Two millimeters more clearance around the cards in the first-print Moss Market base-game tray.
Confirmed in the first-print Moss Market tray proof: two millimeters extra clearance around the sleeved base-game cards is sufficient.

challenges: An unresolved fragment can precede the first named project capture.
One game can have independent development and separately ordered manufacturing projects.
Reused specifications do not merge print orders.
Repeated edits across archive/restore must preserve an explicit correction and revision history.
authorNotes: All game titles, jobs and observations are fictional. The second edit of c01 records confirmation of its existing first-print identity; it never changes membership implicitly.
